novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism-focused representation probe: “whether molecular/materials foundation models represent this selection-rule mechanism rather than treating optical activity as a monotone function of the energy-gap size,” using symmetry-breaking versus symmetry-preserving counterfactuals to separate brightness from gap. The closest works found were “Machine-Learned Electronically Excited States with the MolOrbImage Generated from the Molecular Ground State” (2023), which predicts oscillator strengths without probing internal selection-rule representations, and “Relating Structural and Optical Properties of Organic Thin Films on Chemically Inert Substrates” (2025), which studies symmetry-dependent optical changes but not foundation-model mechanisms; searches used “molecular foundation model interpretability optical selection rules oscillator strength symmetry,” “Laporte rule representation probing,” and “symmetry-breaking counterfactual mechanistic interpretability chemistry.” The step from these works to the claim requires a new core relationship—causal internal representation of parity/spin allowedness independently of the gap—rather than a direct transfer, although the probing, perturbation, and steering techniques themselves are established and the idea does not constitute a general new interpretability paradigm.
